text:
kevin (support): customer ACME hit us — p99 jumped right after canary rollout at ~18:22 UTC. They report 200-300ms -> 1.1-1.4s p99 for text.generate. sample req ids: req-az-1234, req-az-1240. customer started a ticket, asked for ETA.

kevin (support): quick repro curl they gave:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4m-lite","prompt":"short prompt","max_tokens":32}'
```

ow: owen (oncall): thanks — can someone post the canary id & rollout window? I can pull p95/p99 by tenant. Also, any routing overrides?

kevin (support): canary id reported in ticket is canary-2026-03-15-031. rollout started 2026-03-15T18:20:00Z. No tenant-level overrides from support side.

maya (eng-runtime): noted. first suspicion: kernel scheduler change + new batching heuristic landed in that build. pinging lucas to grab tail latency slices. try this prometheus-ish query for quick slice:
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{env="prod",model="gpt-4m-lite"}[5m])) by (le, tenant))
```

lucas (eng-sre): ran quick aggregation for the tenant (acme): last 30m p50~45ms p95~220ms p99~1.25s. baseline (pre-canary) p99 was ~260ms. spike concentrated on requests with seq_len <= 64 and token_count small. looks like a scheduling bump for small requests (small prompt latency tail).

maya (eng-runtime): that pattern matches a scheduler change that prefers larger batches and defers tiny requests a bit — increases tail for low-token requests. commit id: a1b2c3d changed kernel_scheduler->round_robin+batch_reservation.

ow: owen (oncall): can we do a targeted mitigation while we investigate bisect? options: 1) traffic-split this tenant back to stable; 2) toggle runtime flag to disable new scheduler; 3) pin tenant to older runtime version. Which is fastest?

maya (eng-runtime): fastest = traffic-split for the tenant (no full rollback). Command (internal tooling):
```
redwood route update --tenant acme --from canary-2026-03-15-031 --to stable-v3.11 --weight 0.95
```
That routes 95% to stable, keeps 5% on canary for instrumentation. Alternate: flip `enable_kernel_scheduler_v2=false` on canary nodes serving acme, but that's more invasive and needs a quick flag rollout.

kevin (support): i'll ask CS to tell customer we'll route them to stable and monitor. sophie — can you send the heads-up?

sophie (customer-success): on it — messaging: "we're routing your traffic to a stable runtime to restore p99; engineering is bisecting and we'll follow up in 2 hours." leaving a note in the ticket. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary traffic-split job queued: job-id=cs-4923-01, routing change ETA ~30s.

lucas (eng-sre): after routing change (t+6m) acme p99 back to ~260-280ms. I still see a residual 2-3% high-latency on very bursty windows — likely from mixed-pool KV cache coldstarts.

maya (eng-runtime): next steps: bisect scheduler change across smaller commits (a1b2c3d -> a1b2c3d+3). test harness: run 10k synthetic small requests (seq_len 8..64) against candidate builds with `--burst=on --clients=200` and measure p99. I'll own the bisect.

ow: owen (oncall): operational items: 1) keep acme on stable route for 2h, 2) add short-term dashboard for small-request tail by tenant (p95/p99), 3) if bisect identifies single bad commit, prefer revert; if it's heuristic tunable, plan a patch.

kevin (support): customer updated: "thanks, saw immediate improvement". i'll keep them posted.

maya (eng-runtime): filing ticket ENG-RUNTIME-5923 to track bisect + root cause + fix. tagging lucas & owen. will post minimal repro commit hashes & perf numbers there.

ow: lucas (eng-sre): reminder for postmortem if we keep any partial rollout — capture the small-request workload in nightly regression suite.

ow: owen (oncall): good work. If anyone sees regressions resurfacing, escalate here. otherwise i'll close the oncall page in 2h. :white_check_mark:

kevin (support): closing loop with customer now. thanks all. :pray:
